## Active

### D-053 — Kopi generates its own screenshots instead of a demo realm

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-kopi · active_

The screenshot demo first created a throwaway `dev/testrealm` (a rush.json entry plus lockfile
changes), which contradicted the directive not to create new realms. The realm was reverted and
`core/blong-kopi` itself became a runnable realm that generates its own screenshots.

### D-054 — A seed whose method has no handler needs a real handler

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-kopi · active_

The kopi seed crashed because of a stale handler, not because of `$`:
`meta/dbTest/$subject$ObjectMerge.yaml` and `$subjectAuthorizationMerge.yaml` dispatched methods
with no handler, since the master-detail refactor had deleted the custom Add handler.
`$subject$ObjectMerge` resolves through the generic `exec` fallback (like blong-marine's
`marineCoralMerge`), but `$subjectAuthorizationMerge` needed a real handler, so
`adapter/db/$subjectAuthorizationMerge.ts` was added as a simplified `accessAuthorizationMerge`.

### D-055 — The scaffold template reuses the shared RBAC merge handler

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-kopi · active_

The kopi template's `adapter/db/$subjectAuthorizationMerge.ts` was not needed: blong-access's
`accessAuthorizationMerge` handler is fully generic — it processes any
`user`/`role`/`capability`/`policy` names and has no access-specific logic — and it is attached to
the `db` adapter in every suite (access is a child realm, and `srv.db` imports `/.db$/`). The
duplicate existed only because the seed was named `$subjectAuthorizationMerge.yaml`, so its derived
method `$subject.authorization.merge` had no handler; renaming the seed to
`meta/dbTest/accessAuthorizationMerge.yaml` makes the fixed file name derive
`access.authorization.merge` and dispatch to the SHARED handler. Only the seed CONTENT carries
`$subject` placeholders (substituted per realm at scaffold time), so scaffolded realms always reuse
the framework handler and the template stays minimal. Verified: kopi tap 6/6 (RBAC 401/403/200 plus
the permissions assertion) and Playwright 4/4.
